glosses: Short for hooligan (“a young person who causes trouble or violence, typically as a member of a gang or other group”).

examples.text: Hooligans or hoolies are in it for the pure lust of violence and defence of turf and not really politics, although the subculture tends towards a right wing syndrome of working-class machismo and hostility to foreigners and to the better-off, better-dressed, and better-educated. Hoolies also tend towards public inebriation and, sometimes agitated by a small minority screaming 'Sieg Heil' and 'Germany for the Germans', have engaged in massed rampages through towns, attacking shops, police, and whatever target seemed convenient.

In the last published figures for Level Two, The Posh clocked up enough arrests to place them in the top five for hoolie problems for the division, putting them in the same dubious bracket as Stoke and Cardiff.

Offer ten seconds of your morning to make sure a new kid is nerded up nicely and what does he do only try to make himself look cool again! Only nobody is fooled. Not the students and not the teachers and certainly not the hoolies, 'hoolie' being short for ‘hooligan’, Richie Robinson at the helm.

glosses: Alternative spelling of hooley (“a noisy celebration or party”).

examples.text: The celebratory ceilidh at the Culag Hotel in Lochinver is still talked about. 'Oh, it was a fine evening,' one discreet woman said to me. 'A right damn wild hoolie!' a well-oiled friend enthused.

Indeed, our Recording Date was only yesterday and, thanks to a myriad of ongoing so-called technical 'snafus' (more media lingo – you'll get used to it!), we didn't leave the studio (get me, eh?!) until one in the morning, after which our presenters, Jiz and Liz, were in a right fouler, so we all piled back to Jane's gaff for champagne on tap and a wild sort of hoolie that had cocaine and everything, […]

glosses: Alternative spelling of hooley (“a strong wind”).

examples.text: Bertie held mum's hand tightly as the wind was by now blowing a hoolie and Bertie did not feel very safe as he felt that he was close to being blown off his paws on more than one occasion.

I am arriving at the view that we have probably all been battered and bruised by being flung about the cabin as the boat heels over on its ear. We have all felt queasy (at best) when the wind and tide are battling it out in a hoolie and got cold, wet and miserable.
The weather was fine when we first went in but unfortunately it started blowing a ‘hoolie’ in the evening.

glosses: hooligan (“造成麻煩或暴力的年輕人，通常是幫派或其他團體的成員”)之簡寫

examples.text: Hooligans or hoolies are in it for the pure lust of violence and defence of turf and not really politics, although the subculture tends towards a right wing syndrome of working-class machismo and hostility to foreigners and to the better-off, better-dressed, and better-educated. Hoolies also tend towards public inebriation and, sometimes agitated by a small minority screaming 'Sieg Heil' and 'Germany for the Germans', have engaged in massed rampages through towns, attacking shops, police, and whatever target seemed convenient.
examples.translation: 流氓或混混參與其中純粹是為了暴力快感和保衛地盤，而非真正的政治，儘管這種亞文化傾向於工人階級大男子主義和對外國人以及富裕、衣著光鮮、受過良好教育者的敵意的右翼綜合症。小流氓們也傾向於在公共場所醉酒，有時被少數人「勝利萬歲」和「德國屬於德國人」的吶喊煽動，會成群地在城鎮中橫衝直撞，攻擊商店、警察和任何看起來方便的目標。

examples.text: In the last published figures for Level Two, The Posh clocked up enough arrests to place them in the top five for hoolie problems for the division, putting them in the same dubious bracket as Stoke and Cardiff.
examples.translation: 在二級聯賽最後公布的數字中，彼得伯勒聯隊的逮捕數量足以使他們在該級別小流氓問題上排名前五，將他們與斯托克和卡迪夫置於同樣可疑的範疇中。

Not the students and not the teachers and certainly not the hoolies, 'hoolie' being short for ‘hooligan’, Richie Robinson at the helm.
examples.translation: 早上花十秒鐘，確保一個新生裝扮得像書呆子，結果他只會裝酷！誰也不會上當。學生們不會，老師們不會，小流氓們當然也不會，「hoolie」是「hooligan」的簡稱，里奇·羅賓森是頭頭。

glosses: hooley (“喧鬧的慶祝或聚會”)的另一種拼寫法。

examples.text: The celebratory ceilidh at the Culag Hotel in Lochinver is still talked about. 'Oh, it was a fine evening,' one discreet woman said to me. 'A right damn wild hoolie!' a well-oiled friend enthused.
examples.translation: 在洛欣弗的庫拉格酒店舉行的慶祝ceilidh仍然被人們談論。「哦，那是個美好的夜晚，」一位謹慎的女士對我說。「真是個該死的狂野聚會！」一位喝得醉醺醺的朋友熱情地說道。

examples.text: Indeed, our Recording Date was only yesterday and, thanks to a myriad of ongoing so-called technical 'snafus' (more media lingo – you'll get used to it!), we didn't leave the studio (get me, eh?!) until one in the morning, after which our presenters, Jiz and Liz, were in a right fouler, so we all piled back to Jane's gaff for champagne on tap and a wild sort of hoolie that had cocaine and everything, […]
examples.translation: 確實，我們的錄音日期就在昨天，由於無數持續的所謂技術「混亂」（更多媒體術語——你會習慣的！），我們直到凌晨一點才離開錄音室（看我，嗯？！），之後我們的主持人吉茲和莉茲大發雷霆，所以我們都回到簡的家裡暢飲香檳，舉行狂野的聚會，有可卡因和一切， […]

examples.text: Bertie held mum's hand tightly as the wind was by now blowing a hoolie and Bertie did not feel very safe as he felt that he was close to being blown off his paws on more than one occasion.
examples.translation: 伯蒂緊緊握住媽媽的手，因為此時狂風已經颳得很猛烈，伯蒂感到不太安全，因為他不只一次覺得自己差點被吹掉爪子。

examples.text: I am arriving at the view that we have probably all been battered and bruised by being flung about the cabin as the boat heels over on its ear. We have all felt queasy (at best) when the wind and tide are battling it out in a hoolie and got cold, wet and miserable.
examples.translation: 我開始認為我們可能都曾在船艙裡被拋來拋去而被撞得傷痕累累，因為船隻側傾得厲害。當風和潮汐在狂風中較量時，我們都感到噁心（至少如此），變得寒冷、濕漉漉和痛苦。

examples.text: The weather was fine when we first went in but unfortunately it started blowing a ‘hoolie’ in the evening.
examples.translation: 我們第一次進去時天氣很好，但不幸的是晚上開始颳狂風。
